newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese pound continues rise against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese pound continues rise against dollar.

text.p: The Lebanese pound continued its rise against the dollar in the week ended on Friday, and dealers said the market was relatively active.

The Bank of Lebanon lowered its bid-offer intervention band to 1,541.5-1,551 pounds per dollar from 1,542-1,551.5 last week and the dollar traded at the bottom of the band throughout the week, dealers said.

Talal Abou Zaki, Manager of Forex Money market for Bank of Beirut and the Arab Countries, said trade was restricted to a tight range of up to 1.5 Lebanese pound at the bid end of the intervention band.
There was some demand for dollars but all was met by the banks, he said.
The market was active as there were dollar offers on the first two days of the week and many demand orders on Thursday and Friday, he added.

"The offers of commercial banks for dollars at the first two days of the week converted to become demand orders at the last two days because one bank opened the subscription for a capital increase," Abou Zaki said.
